To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified several transcription factors that characterize different neuronal subpopulates generated in vitro from ES cell.
we have characterized neuronal subpopulations from in vitro ES cell differentiation, by using as markers the homeoproteins expression.

we have developed a method for the generation of specific neuronal subtypes from ES cells, that we have used this method to generate neurons of all three major neuronal lineages, and that these neurons express combinations of homeodomain transcription factor markers characteristic of specific neuronal lineages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and functional characterization of neuronal subtypes generated from embryonic stem cells.
the development of a novel approach for the generation of defined neuronal populations from embryonic stem cells.
the generation of neuronal cells from ES cells, the molecular characterization and the differentiation of these neuronal cells in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuronal subpopulations that can be generated from embryonic stem cells in vitro are very similar to those that are found in the embryo.
ES cells can be induced to differentiate into a wide spectrum of CNS neurons.
the neuronal subpopulations that are derived from ES cells express combinations of transcription factors characteristic of motoneuron and interneuron lineages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ES cells have the capacity to generate neurons that resemble those of the CNS and PNS.
ES cell-derived neurons express a combination of markers that are characteristic of different neuronal subpoputions.

we have been able to generate a large variety of neurons from mouse ES cells, which can be used for studying the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal development, and for the generation of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of neurological diseases and injuries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ES cells can be used to produce large numbers of neurons and glia for research and possibly clinical applications.
the molecular characterization of neurons derived from ES cells can be used to define the molecular identity of different neuron populations.
we can now generate neurons that are similar to those found in the developing brain and spinal cord.
